narr: During the afternoon and evening of the 18th, a few rounds of thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall to much of northern Illinois resulting in flash flooding. One particularly strong storm also produced damaging winds in DeKalb County. Initial reports estimate $8.8 million in flood damages around northern and northeast Illinois, and around $2.5 million in the city of Chicago alone.
ev: An NWS employee reported 1 to 1.5 feet of standing water at the intersection of Naper Blvd and 87 St just south of the Will/DuPage county line. Water was encroaching on driveways nearby. At least six inches of flowing water were reported at Arlington Ave and River Woods Dr. A couple of mPing reports of street flooding were also received from the same area.
Photos shared via social media showed 6 to 8 inches of water on Washington St in Darien, with flooding also impacting homes.
A report of flooding was received from northeast of Creston via mPing.
A report of flooding was received out of La Salle via mPing.
A report was received of 1 to 2 feet of water on Gartner Rd in Naperville with vehicles stranded.
Street flooding was reported on the southeast side of Yorkville with at least six inches of standing water. A few other mPing reports of street flooding came out of the Yorkville and Oswego areas.
In Downers Grove, 6 to 8 inches of water were reported flowing over Belmont Rd near 59th St. Street flooding was also reported near 55th St via mPing.
A report was received via mPing of street flooding north of 55th St west of Fairview Ave in Downers Grove.

Flash flooding impacted portions of far northeast Winnebago County, specifically in the vicinity of Rockton. Street flooding was reported near Rockton Rd and Dorr Rd with floodwater reaching into yards. Street flooding was also reported via mPing along I-39 south of McCurry Rd. A private weather station on the east side of Rockton recorded 4.5 of rainfall. Two others nearby recorded closer to 3.5.
A video shared to social media showed at least a foot of water flowing over Chicago Rd east of Paw Paw.
A report of flooding was received from the northwest side of DeKalb via mPing.
An estimated 500 structures flooded around the city of Chicago causing approximately $2.5 million in damages.

Extensive flash flooding was reported around southern Cook County. Numerous reports of street and basement flooding came out of Orland Hills, Midlothian, Homer Glen, and Tinley Park. At least one foot of water was reported along 183rd and 179th streets near LaGrange Rd. In Orland Park, 143rd St near Creek Crossing Dr was closed due to flooding. Wolf Rd was flooded near 167th St near the Marley Creek crossing in Homer Glen. One Cocorahs observer in Midlothian recorded 5.7 of 24-hour rainfall the next morning with several other reports in the area between 3 and 4. Damage estimates around the area come in at $1.5 million with roughly 300 structures flooded.

An estimated 700 structures were flooded in southeast Cook County, including Dolton, Harvey, South Holland, and Thornton. Two lanes of I-294 near the quarry in Thornton were covered in water. Damages in the area are estimated at around $3.5 million.

Numerous reports of street flooding came out of the east side of Mokena, south of I-80. Near the Hickory Creek train station, at least 6 inches of water were flooding a viaduct. Up to 3 feet of water were reported on a roadway near Hercht Park. A nearby private weather station recorded 3.62 inches of rain from approximately 6 to 9 PM CST. Reports show flooding began in the area following an initial push of heavy rain during the 6PM CST hour, with additional flooding following subsequent storms through the evening. An estimated 200 structures were flooded around the Mokena, Frankfort, and Crete areas totaling around $1 million in flood damages.

A couple of rounds of torrential rainfall brought flash flooding to parts of southeast Lee County. A video shared to social media showed a house in the Paw Paw area surrounded by floodwater with significant flooding in the yard and in nearby fields. Paw Paw Rd was flooded approximately one mile north of Paw Paw. In Compton, water was seen flowing over roads and parking lots. A private weather station in Paw Paw recorded 7.02 of storm total rain, 5.03 of which fell between 3:15 and 5:15 CST. Another private weather station near Dunn Airport northwest of Paw Paw recorded 4.67 of storm total rainfall. The flooding is estimated to have resulted in $5,000 worth of damages, mostly to crops.

Numerous reports of street, yard, and basement flooding came out of the Joliet, Crest Hill, Lockport, and Homer Glen areas. In Homer Glen, a video shared via social media showed 1 to 2 feet of standing water on a residential street southwest of 167th St and Cedar Rd. Around 50 flooded structures were estimated amounting to roughly $250,000 in damages.
